model.name: Organization
model.purpose: Identity, legal form, registration, classification, purpose, presence and subject-level lifecycle of any organization that can act under a shared name.
model.scope_statement: This model is the format-neutral subject record for an organization as a collective agent: a grouping of people or institutions with a purpose beyond its current members, whether or not it is a registered legal entity. It is the identity anchor referenced by nearly every other catalogue model. It covers who the organization is, how it is named and identified, how it is classified, how it is recorded in registers, what standing it currently has, how it came into being, transformed or ceased, what it declares as purpose, and where it can be reached. Internal structure (units and teams), employment, beneficial ownership, constitutive charter text, geospatial address objects, accounting documents and access-grant machinery are sibling or contained models, not duplicated here.
in_scope: Named collectives that can act as agents, including companies, partnerships, cooperatives, non-profits, charities, clubs, churches, communities, public institutions, government units, international organizations, funds, sole proprietors acting in a business capacity, and unregistered informal organizations.
Legal, trading, former and transliterated names with language and validity.
Scheme-issued identifiers including national registry numbers, LEI, tax and other identifiers, treated as structured identifier records.
Legal form under a home jurisdiction, aligned to ISO 20275 ELF and national form lists.
Economic activity classification aligned to ISIC and regional implementations such as NACE.
Entity category distinctions used in the Global LEI System: general entity, branch, fund, sole proprietor, resident government entity, international organization.
Formal registration entries, home legal jurisdiction, entity status and identifier-registration status.
Founding and creation dates, legal-entity events, mergers, splits, conversions, successor links and dissolution.
Declared purpose or objects and public presence points: registered site, headquarters, other sites and contact channels.
Record stewardship of the organization subject itself, as distinct from internal officer employment.
out_of_scope: Organizational units, departments and posts that exist only inside a parent organization (WM-ORG-002 and W3C org:OrganizationalUnit / org:Post).
Person membership, employment contracts, remuneration, reporting lines and role taxonomies as staffing (W3C org:Membership, org:Role, org:headOf).
Beneficial ownership, shareholding, direct and ultimate parent control, and GLEIF Level 2 relationship records.
Constitutive charter, articles, bylaws and powers text.
The public register as a first-class institution.
Geospatial address, cadastral and location geometry objects beyond a presence locator pointing at a location sibling.
Accounting documents, financial statements and audit reports as a financial-reporting model.
Products, brands, offers, payments and merchant policies.
Sanctions, fitness-and-propriety and watchlist membership as a dedicated model.
Natural persons except as referenced founders, officers-as-stewards or agents of the record.

boundary_notes.distinction: W3C org:Organization is broader than a registered legal entity and is the correct outer class for informal clubs and communities; rov:RegisteredOrganization and SEMIC Legal Entity are profiles of formally registered trading bodies and must not be treated as the whole model.
A legally distinct subsidiary is another Organization instance linked by succession or group relations, not an OrganizationalUnit.

boundary_notes.neighbor: GLEIF BRANCH entity category and org:Site
boundary_notes.distinction: An international branch may be an LEI-eligible entity category without being a separate incorporated company; that is not the same as org:Site.
Group ownership and control are sibling facts. Officers who sign for the record are stewardship actors, not employment facts.

boundary_notes.neighbor: ISO 17442, ISO 20275, NACE, ISIC and W3C ORG as instruments
boundary_notes.distinction: No claim is made that this model conforms to ISO 17442, ISO 20275, NACE, ISIC or W3C ORG; those instruments are alignments. ELF coverage is incomplete for some jurisdictions (reserved codes 8888 and 9999).

boundary_notes.neighbor: Forms and events lacking a primary cross-jurisdictional schema
boundary_notes.distinction: Restoration after strike-off, cross-border redomiciliation, name reservation, series LLCs, DAOs and indigenous nations as polities lack a single primary cross-jurisdictional schema and are recorded as gaps rather than canonical nodes.

bundles.name: Identity
bundles.description: Establish who the organization is as a subject: formality class, names over time, and scheme-issued identifiers, without collapsing informal collectives into registered companies.
bundles.rationale: Groups the naming, identifiers and entity-kind layers, which together answer who the subject is before any classification, registration or lifecycle fact is attached.

layers.name: Naming
layers.description: Capture legal, trading, former and transliterated names with language and validity, including the multilingual-legal-name case that ORG under-specifies.

findings.name: Legal and official names
findings.description: A registered organization has at least one legal name as recorded in an official register or constituting documents. In jurisdictions with more than one official language there may be several legal names of equal standing. W3C ORG recommends a single skos:prefLabel for the legally recognized name; RegOrg and the Core Business Vocabulary therefore introduce legalName as a repeatable literal with language tags. LEI-CDF 3.1 records one Primary LegalName plus OtherEntityNames.

findings.description: Organizations commonly carry trading names, doing-business-as names, colloquial names and retired former names. RegOrg and CBV record these as alternative names and forbid using alternative-name fields for translations of the legal name. LEI-CDF 3.1 provides OtherEntityNames and TransliteratedOtherEntityNames. LEI ROC policy treats change of legal name or trade name as a legal-entity event that must keep history. Some jurisdictions treat use of a non-legal name as suspicious.

layers.name: Identifiers
layers.description: Represent scheme-issued identifiers as first-class records, distinguishing the legal-status identifier from other identifiers and from a Dimension-assigned UUID.

findings.name: Scheme-issued identifiers
findings.description: An organization is identified by one or more scheme-issued identifiers. ORG encodes identifier as a typed literal (sub-property of skos:notation). Registered-organization profiles require a structured Identifier (ADMS/UN-CEFACT) with notation, issuing agency, scheme name or URI, and issue date, because the legal identifier confers status and must be described. CBV distinguishes legal identifier (issued by the authority that conferred legal status) from other identifiers such as tax numbers. schema.org additionally surfaces DUNS, VAT, taxID and ISO 6523. Identity priority is: authoritative master-system identifier in the home register; then a governed global identifier such as LEI; then a UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension. A date is not an identifier.

findings.name: LEI and other global schemes
findings.description: ISO 17442 defines a 20-character Legal Entity Identifier with no embedded intelligence for parties that are legally or financially responsible or that can enter contracts, including some unincorporated forms. GLEIF LEI-CDF 3.1 is the operational Level 1 record. An LEI is unique and exclusive: it is never reassigned, and a legal entity must not hold two surviving LEIs. Registration status of the LEI (ISSUED, LAPSED, DUPLICATE, RETIRED, ANNULLED, CANCELLED, TRANSFERRED and pending states) is distinct from the entity's legal operating status. schema.org leiCode and ISO 6523 ICD 0199 are projections of the same scheme.

layers.name: Entity kind
layers.description: Distinguish informal organizations, formal organizations and registered legal entities, and record LEI entity categories that change identifier and relationship rules.

findings.name: Organization formality spectrum
findings.description: org:Organization is a collection of people with a common purpose that can act as an agent, including informal communities. org:FormalOrganization is recognized in the world at large, especially in legal jurisdictions, with rights and responsibilities (corporation, charity, government, church). rov:RegisteredOrganization / CBV Legal Entity is a formal organization that gained legal status through a registration process and excludes natural persons, virtual organizations and agents that can act without that registration. Many organizations are not legal entities; some umbrellas contain several legal entities. Unregistered collectives remain in scope of this model as Organization, not as RegisteredOrganization.

bundles.description: Classify the organization by legal form, economic activity and sector without treating those schemes as interchangeable.

layers.name: Legal form
layers.description: Record the jurisdiction-bound legal form using ISO 20275 ELF where available, plus the national form vocabulary actually used by the home register.

findings.name: ELF code assignment
findings.description: ISO 20275 defines entity legal form as the type of entity an organization is considered to be within the legal or regulatory system under which it is formed, including unincorporated forms. GLEIF publishes the ELF Code List (v1.6, February 2026: 3600+ forms, 200+ jurisdictions). An ELF code is four Latin alphanumeric characters and contains no embedded intelligence. Forms are published in local official languages only; a Dutch BV is not a German GmbH. Reserved code 8888 is used while a new form is requested; 9999 is used when the entity has no separate legal form. Legal form is dependent on LegalJurisdiction in LEI-CDF.

questions.text: What ISO 20275 ELF code and local-language legal form name apply in the home jurisdiction, and which ELF list version was used?

ELF is the cross-border alignment, not a replacement for the national register's form code when that register is the master system.

findings.name: ISIC and NACE activity codes
findings.description: Activity is classified using a controlled vocabulary. ISIC is the UN international standard; ISIC Rev. 5 was endorsed in 2023 while Rev. 4 remains widely deployed. NACE is the EU implementation; NACE Rev. 2 applies to European statistics 2008-2024 and NACE Rev. 2.1, adopted 2022 and in force for statistics from 2025, is the European implementation of ISIC Rev. 5. RegOrg and CBV prefer NACE for European interoperability and accept national schemes such as UK SIC that map to ISIC. schema.org still cites ISIC Rev. 4 as a text field. Codes from different revisions are not interchangeable without correspondence tables.

findings.description: Registers typically record one or more activities. Statistical classification of an enterprise uses a primary activity (the activity that contributes most to value added) and may record secondary activities. CBV legal entity activity is repeatable. Treating every registered code as primary breaks statistical and risk use.

composition.purpose: An organization instance contains organizational-unit instances that have meaning only inside this organization and are not separate legal entities. Rationale: W3C org:hasUnit / org:OrganizationalUnit; structural matryoshka recorded in known relations.

An organization instance contains team instances as operational groups. Teams are not legal entities and are not a substitute for units. Rationale: operational matryoshka recorded in known relations; ORG unit/post coverage does not itself define teams, so this remains a catalogue containment rather than a W3C class equivalence.

An organization may contain or link to other organization subjects that are themselves legal entities, for example subsidiaries. Those peers are Organization instances, not units. Ownership percentages live in a control sibling. Rationale: org:hasSubOrganization allows FormalOrganization to contain FormalOrganization; this is identity linking, while control is out of scope.

Align classes and properties to org:Organization, org:FormalOrganization, org:identifier, org:purpose, org:classification, org:Site and org:ChangeEvent without requiring RDF storage. Rationale: W3C ORG is the broad organization ontology; this model is broader than registered business only.

When the subject is a registered legal entity, align to rov:RegisteredOrganization, rov:legalName, rov:registration, rov:orgType, rov:orgStatus and rov:orgActivity. Rationale: RegOrg is the registered-entity profile of ORG and must not be applied to informal collectives.

Align registered legal-entity fields to CBV Legal Entity, legal identifier versus identifier, legal form type, status, activity, registered address and contact point. Rationale: SEMIC CBV is the EU Core Vocabulary used in BRIS-oriented interchange.

Use LEI and LEI-CDF Level 1 as a governed global identifier and who-is-who record, including events and successor links. Level 2 parent relationships are not imported. Rationale: ISO 17442 and GLEIF CDF are the global legal-entity identifier system.

Legal form codes are drawn from the GLEIF-maintained ISO 20275 ELF list for the home jurisdiction. Rationale: ELF is the cross-border legal-form code list; national form codes remain master in home registers.

Activity classifications reference ISIC and, where EU interoperability is required, NACE, with explicit scheme version. Rationale: UN ISIC and Eurostat NACE are the primary activity schemes cited by RegOrg and CBV.

Presence points store kind and validity here and point at address records in a location sibling (locn/INSPIRE/vCard), rather than duplicating geospatial address semantics. Rationale: CBV and ORG both defer detailed address structure to location vocabularies.

Purpose statements and objects clauses may cite a charter or constituting instrument; the instrument body is not stored here. Rationale: previous-version composition to world.charter; constitutive rules are a sibling concern.

Person-to-organization membership, posts and employment resolve against this identity; they are not attributes of the organization subject. Rationale: W3C Membership/Post/Role are explicitly out of this model's operating surface.
Registry entries anchor to publicly or privately kept registers modelled elsewhere. Rationale: the register is a different subject from the organization recorded in it.

Ownership of the organization data record and access grants are governed by stewardship and access-grant siblings; this model only names steward roles and projection rules. Rationale: catalogue S1/S2 separation means this model must not re-implement grants.

Lifecycle events and standing changes carry audit facets (actor, recorded time, evidence) from a shared audit-trail mix-in. Rationale: ORG uses PROV-O on ChangeEvent; ROC requires data history; a shared mix-in avoids a private audit schema.

owner_package_requirements: The Dimension operator assigns Dimension UUIDs or ULIDs and may do so only after scheme-issued identifiers have been searched for duplicates.
The Dimension operator enforces the integrity rules and the retention rule, and may not silently overwrite master-system legal names or legal identifiers.
The Dimension operator runs the AGENTS.md bootstrap, storage and interfaces without becoming the legal master of the record.
dimension.namespace_guidance: The model is registered as vr.wm-org-001 under model id WM-ORG-001; Dimension-assigned UUIDs or ULIDs live in the adopting Dimension's namespace and never replace scheme-issued identifiers, which stay in their issuing scheme's namespace (home register, LEI, ISO 6523 ICD).
registry_links: Catalogue registry entry vr.wm-org-001 for WM-ORG-001 Organization.
GLEIF Registration Authorities List (RACL) codes used as register identifiers.
GLEIF-maintained ISO 20275 ELF Code List (v1.6) used for legal-form codes.

canonicalization_rules: Name strings are stored as recorded, without normalization that would destroy legal spelling.
Identifier notations preserve the canonical formatting rules of their issuing scheme.
Legal form is always stored with its jurisdiction, and activity codes are always stored with scheme and revision.
One organization subject has at most one surviving canonical identifier per identifier scheme.
patch_rules: Name, address, form, status and activity updates are applied through a legal-entity event with separate effective and recorded timestamps.
Master-system fields (home-register legal name, legal identifier, ELF in jurisdiction) change only with registrar or LOU evidence.
Self-declared purpose and public contact channels may be updated by the steward without a register extract.
Annulled or duplicate identifier records are marked, not erased, so exclusivity violations remain auditable.
compatibility_rules: Deprecated LEI-CDF constructs (MERGED registration status, EntityExpirationDate/Reason, AssociatedEntity) are retained only for compatibility and are replaced by events and successor entities.
Codes from different ISIC or NACE revisions are not interchangeable without correspondence tables.
Alignment to ORG, RegOrg, CBV, ISO 17442, ISO 20275, ISIC and NACE is not conformance, and conformance is not claimed without a recorded evidence artifact.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier in the home register.
A governed global identifier such as the LEI.
A UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension.
A date is not an identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Timestamps are RFC 3339 values with seconds and an explicit offset, carrying stated precision when the source publishes only a date; event effective time, recorded time and ingestion time are stored as separate RFC 3339 values.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Artifacts are not serially numbered by this model; where a source register, LOU or event record issues its own extract, case or event number, that number is preserved as recorded rather than replaced.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: One organization subject has at most one surviving canonical identifier per identifier scheme; a duplicate LEI or register number is a status of an identifier record, not a second subject. EntityStatus, identifier RegistrationStatus and national standing codes must never be stored in a single status field. Legal form is always stored with its jurisdiction. Activity codes are always stored with scheme and revision. Event effective time and recorded/ingestion time are separate RFC 3339 values. Informal organizations must not be coerced into a fake company number.

policies: Treat W3C ORG, RegOrg, CBV, ISO 17442, ISO 20275, ISIC and NACE as alignments; do not claim conformance without a recorded evidence artifact.
Public directory projections omit identifier history, non-public contact channels and internal purpose drafts; compliance projections require an admitted requester and an audit record.
Dissolution retires the subject but does not reuse identifiers and does not by itself delete lineage.
Stewards of the record are the organization via officers plus named registrars for their copies; Dimension operators may not silently overwrite master-system legal names or legal identifiers.

read: Any admitted agent may resolve public directory-card fields.
Compliance-profile and full identifier history require a grant or a statutory register right.
Lineage view is readable whenever the requester can read the subject or a successor.
create: Create is allowed when a home-register extract, LEI record, or explicit informal-organization declaration with evidence is supplied.
A Dimension UUID/ULID may be assigned only after scheme-issued identifiers have been searched for duplicates.
Creation of a RegisteredOrganization profile requires a legal identifier that confers status.
update: Name, address, form, status and activity updates should be applied through a legal-entity event with effective and recorded timestamps.
Master-system fields (home-register legal name, legal identifier, ELF in jurisdiction) change only with registrar or LOU evidence.
Self-declared purpose and public contact channels may be updated by the steward without a register extract.
delete: Hard delete is forbidden while successor resolution or a legal hold depends on the identifier.
Soft-retire after dissolution according to the retention rule.
Annulled or duplicate identifier records are marked, not erased, so exclusivity violations remain auditable.

coverage.claim: This structure covers the defensible identity, classification, registration, lifecycle and presence surface of organizations from W3C ORG/RegOrg, SEMIC CBV, ISO 17442/LEI-CDF 3.1, ISO 20275 ELF, UN ISIC and Eurostat NACE, including informal collectives and rare LEI statuses, while leaving units, teams, employment, ownership, charters and location geometry to siblings. It is not a universal ontology of every legal system.

checklist.notes: Names, structured identifiers, LEI, formality classes and Dimension UUID priority are modelled with primary sources.
Creation, legal-entity events, succession, dissolution, lapsed/retired/annulled identifier states and data history are covered; restoration and redomiciliation are hooked as gaps.
Successor/predecessor, umbrella-to-legal-entity, branch-to-headquarters and containment of units/teams are covered; ownership/control is explicitly sibling.
RFC 3339 effective versus recorded versus ingestion times are required on names, status, events and presence.
Validation sources, validation authorities, documents and registrar versus self-declared assignment sources are in registration and event findings.
Beneficial ownership and parent control are GLEIF Level 2 / company-law siblings; only record-stewardship of the identity is in scope.
LEI ValidationSources, national standing corroboration and quality exceptions are first-class.
Public, compliance and lineage projections plus default-deny and statutory-register exceptions are specified in record-governance and service layers.
Dissolution retains lineage; identifiers are never reused; hard delete is exceptional and must not break resolution.
Alignments to ORG, RegOrg, CBV, LEI, ELF, ISIC/NACE and ISO 6523/schema.org discovery are recorded with explicit non-conformance.
Legal form (ELF and national), activity (ISIC/NACE with revision) and taxonomic schemes are separated.
Registered office, headquarters, other sites and contact channels are locators; geometry is sibling.
W3C Organization without registration is in scope; fake company numbers are forbidden by integrity rule.

known_omissions: Cross-border redomiciliation/continuation as a standardized event type.
Restoration after administrative strike-off as a global code.
Name reservation and companies in formation before legal personality.
Series LLCs, protected-cell companies and similar internal liability partitions.
DAOs and smart-contract collectives without a register or LEI-eligible contract capacity.
Indigenous nations and polities as sovereigns rather than organizations.
GLEIF RR-CDF Level 2 parent, fund-relationship and reporting-exception records.
Officer/director registers as a governance model (ISO 5009 roles discovered but not fetched as a governing source).
NAICS as a first-party Bureau source was not fetched; North American activity is a likely regional omission.
Core Public Organisation Vocabulary is a specialized public-body profile not fully expanded here.
conflicts: W3C ORG recommends one legally recognized skos:prefLabel; RegOrg and CBV allow multiple legalName values in multilingual jurisdictions; LEI-CDF allows one Primary LegalName plus OtherEntityNames.
ORG identifier is a typed literal; RegOrg/CBV require a structured ADMS Identifier; both can be derived in one direction only.
LEI EntityStatus, LEI RegistrationStatus and national orgStatus vocabularies are three different state machines often wrongly merged.
NACE Rev. 2, NACE Rev. 2.1, ISIC Rev. 4 and ISIC Rev. 5 are related but not interchangeable; schema.org still cites ISIC Rev. 4.
ELF codes are unique per jurisdiction-form pair; similarly named forms (SA, LLC, GmbH) are not equivalent across borders.
AssociatedEntity is deprecated in LEI-CDF 3.1 in favour of events and relationship records.
A GLEIF BRANCH category is not an org:OrganizationalUnit and not necessarily an org:Site.
CBV/RegOrg exclude informal organizations that W3C ORG and this catalogue purpose explicitly include.
regional_assumptions: Home legal jurisdiction can be expressed as ISO 3166-1 or 3166-2.
Where a business register exists, it is the master for legal name, legal identifier and national legal form.
EU interoperability prefers NACE; global statistical comparison prefers ISIC; other regions use national schemes mapped to ISIC.
LEI is widely available for contract-capable entities but is not mandatory for all organization types or informal collectives.
ELF list v1.6 still uses reserved 8888/9999 where research is incomplete, including some legal forms not yet enumerated.
French overseas territories sharing French legislation inherit French ELF codes and legal jurisdiction France, per GLEIF ELF notes.
Public access to company extracts varies; UK/EU open-register practice must not be assumed for all states.
adversarial_checks: Informal community versus registered company: refusing a fake company number while still assigning a Dimension id and names.
Lapsed LEI versus dissolved entity: a non-renewed identifier must not be treated as cessation.
Duplicate LEI exclusivity violation: DUPLICATE status marks the non-surviving identifier, not a second organization.
International branch with own LEI versus a mere site of headquarters.
Merger where the surviving legal entity keeps its id versus a new entity that must receive a new canonical id.
Two official legal names in a bilingual jurisdiction versus a translation stored as a trading name.
Subsidiary that is a full Organization versus a department modelled as WM-ORG-002.
Government ministry that can contract without incorporation, eligible for LEI as RESIDENT_GOVERNMENT_ENTITY.
Sole proprietor where the human person is a sibling and only the business capacity is this subject.
Activity code copied from an old NACE Rev. 2 filing after the statistical program moved to Rev. 2.1 without correspondence.
